summary: All 59 tests across the three new files map 1:1 to the TDD anchors in tasks/3.md and exercise meaningful behavior — the litmus test holds for every assertion that matters (Decision 14 deletedAt-FIRST guard, mass-assignment defense, restore-suffix metadata, anti-enumeration parity across all four verbs, audit-event metadata content for project_renamed/updated/restored). The code-side assertions are crisp: 409s assert `code == "project_name_taken"`, 422s assert `code == "project_limit_reached"`, 404s assert status only (correct for AC-T1 since GlobalErrorHandler emits `code: null` for 404). Real concerns: (1) the 401-bare-client test does NOT use a bare client and silently relaxes 4 of 6 verbs to `is4xxClientError`, leaving CSRF-vs-auth ordering — and AC-11 itself — partly unverified; (2) the `$.ownerId.doesNotExist()` response-shape lock is missing on six PATCH/RESTORE happy-path bodies (PATCH no-name-change, PATCH no-op same-name, PATCH blank description, PATCH blank timezone, RESTORE happy, RESTORE collision); (3) `Thread.sleep(10)` in `getProjects_returnsOnlyOwnActiveSortedDesc` is brittle and replaceable. Tone-wise these are upgrades, not blockers — coverage of the security-critical primitives is solid.

findings.issue: `anyEndpoint_unauthenticatedBareClient_returns401` does not match the contract its name advertises (and that AC-11 + tasks/3.md anchor lines 65-66 + 123 explicitly require). Two issues. (a) **Not bare.** It reuses the inherited `webTestClient` from `AbstractIntegrationTest`, which is the same client every other test uses with `@WithMockAppUser`. The task said: `WebTestClient.bindToApplicationContext(applicationContext).build()` — a fresh, unmutated client to ensure no stale `SecurityContext` or test-only mutator is in play. The current test happens to work because `@WithMockAppUser` is method-level and absent here, but the design intent ("prove the auth filter, not the test wiring, returns 401") is not pinned. (b) **Relaxes 4 of 6 verbs to `is4xxClientError`.** The two GETs assert `isUnauthorized` (401); POST, PATCH, DELETE, POST-restore assert only `is4xxClientError`, which silently accepts 403 from the CSRF filter. The inline comment acknowledges this and treats CSRF-first as an acceptable substitute, but AC-11 mandates 401 specifically and Decision 2 (anti-enumeration) requires the auth gate to fire **before** any other gate so an unauthenticated probe cannot distinguish CSRF-protected from CSRF-exempt endpoints by status code. As written, if `SecurityConfig` were inverted to put `.csrf()` before `.authorizeExchange()` and the auth filter never fired for state-changing verbs, this test would still pass — exactly the regression AC-11 is meant to catch.
findings.fix: Two-step fix. (1) Build a bare client at the top of the method (matches the task spec): `WebTestClient bare = WebTestClient.bindToApplicationContext(applicationContext).build();` (inject `ApplicationContext applicationContext` via `@Autowired` on the class — `AbstractIntegrationTest` already has it autowired in nearby tests; confirm). (2) For each state-changing verb, pre-attach the csrf mutator so the CSRF filter is satisfied and the auth filter wins: `bare.mutateWith(csrf()).post().uri("/api/v1/projects").contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).bodyValue(Map.of("name","Acme","timezone","Europe/Kyiv")).exchange().expectStatus().isUnauthorized();` Repeat for PATCH/DELETE/POST-restore. After this change the test asserts 401 on all six verbs (matches AC-11 wording) and proves auth-before-CSRF in the filter chain. Keep the two GET arms as-is (no csrf mutator needed for safe verbs).

findings.issue: Response-shape lock (`$.ownerId.doesNotExist()`) is missing on six handlers that return a `ProjectResponse`. Tech-spec line 320 mandates: "same assertion repeated for GET, PATCH, RESTORE responses." Currently asserted on: POST happy (105), POST hostile (267), GET-list row 0 (299), PATCH rename happy (481), DELETE happy (596). Currently NOT asserted on: (a) `patchProject_noNameChange_emitsProjectUpdatedWithoutNameInMetadata` (line 501 — only `expectStatus().isOk()`, no body assertions); (b) `patchProject_noOpRenameSameName_returns200` (line 539 — asserts `$.name` but not `$.ownerId`); (c) `patchProject_blankDescription_setsDbDescriptionToNull` (line 561 — only status); (d) `patchProject_blankTimezone_doesNotOverwriteExistingTimezone` (line 577 — only status); (e) `restoreProject_happyPath_returns200AndEmitsProjectRestored` (lines 637-640 assert `$.deletedAt.doesNotExist` and `$.name` but not `$.ownerId`); (f) `restoreProject_withNameCollision_appendsSuffixAndSetsRenamedDueToConflictMetadata` (lines 659-661 assert `$.name` only). The IT also has no GET-single happy-path test that asserts `$.ownerId.doesNotExist` against a real response (the slice test does, but slice uses a mocked service and doesn't exercise the real entity-→-DTO mapping). If a future refactor changes `ProjectResponse` to include `ownerId` (or if `toResponse` accidentally serializes the full entity), only the POST/GET-list/PATCH-rename/DELETE paths catch it; the PATCH-update/RESTORE/PATCH-blank paths silently leak it.
findings.fix: Add `.jsonPath("$.ownerId").doesNotExist()` to the existing `expectBody()` chains on all six tests above (a-f). For the four PATCH tests that currently end at `.expectStatus().isOk()` with no body block, append `.expectBody().jsonPath("$.ownerId").doesNotExist()`. For the two RESTORE tests, slot the assertion alongside the existing `$.name` / `$.deletedAt` lines. Additionally, add a dedicated `getProject_singleHappyPath_returns200WithProjectResponseShape` IT test (parallel to the slice test but exercising the real DB → entity → DTO path) that asserts the full ProjectResponse JSON shape including `$.ownerId.doesNotExist()`. This gives the response-shape lock end-to-end teeth: any refactor that serializes the Project entity directly would fail in IT, not silently pass through the slice test's mocked path.

findings.issue: `getProjects_returnsOnlyOwnActiveSortedDesc` uses `Thread.sleep(10)` between two `saveActive` calls to force `createdAt`-desc ordering. Two problems: (a) on a busy CI runner with coarse-grained `Instant.now()` resolution (some Linux kernels expose `Instant.now()` at millisecond granularity, others at microsecond — Java guarantees only millisecond per `Instant#now` Javadoc), 10ms may collapse to identical millis and the sort tie-break is repository-implementation-defined; (b) it's a sleep-in-a-test smell that the codebase otherwise avoids (audit-event polling uses `await().atMost(...)` — deterministic). The fact that the test currently passes is luck-of-the-clock, not a contract.
findings.fix: Drop `Thread.sleep` and assign explicit `createdAt` values when seeding, then assert on either name order (current) or createdAt order. Replace `saveActive(USER_ID, "A")` / sleep / `saveActive(USER_ID, "B")` with: `Project a = new Project(); a.setOwnerId(USER_ID); a.setName("A"); a.setTimezone("Europe/Kyiv"); a.setCreatedAt(Instant.parse("2026-05-10T10:00:00Z")); a.setUpdatedAt(a.getCreatedAt()); projectRepository.save(a).block();` and a parallel `b` with `2026-05-10T10:00:01Z`. Now the desc sort is deterministic regardless of clock resolution. Bonus: extract a `saveActiveAt(ownerId, name, createdAt)` helper next to `saveActive` for any future ordering tests.

findings.issue: `restoreProject_onActiveProject_returns404AndDoesNotEmitRenameOrRestoreEvent` correctly asserts that no `project_renamed` or `project_restored` event exists for `active.getId()`, which is exactly what Decision 14's deletedAt-FIRST guard requires. However, the assertion does not check that `project_updated` / `project_soft_deleted` events are also absent for this projectId. The deletedAt-FIRST guard is supposed to short-circuit BEFORE the save call, so no event of any project_* type should be written for this id (the event chain runs in `.doOnSuccess(saved -> ...)`, which never fires when the upstream errors). Also: the test checks event presence against `e.getMetadata().get("projectId")` but does not first scope the filter to events whose `userId == USER_ID` — in a multi-user-seed test this could false-positive on metadata collision (low risk here because only USER_ID is seeded, but the assertion shape leaves room for future regression).
findings.fix: Tighten the assertion to assert no project_* event at all for this projectId: `assertThat(all).noneMatch(e -> e.getEventType().startsWith("project_") && active.getId().equals(e.getMetadata() == null ? null : e.getMetadata().get("projectId")));` This locks the broader contract (no mutation, no event) in one line. Optional cleanup: factor a small helper `private boolean eventMatches(Event e, String type, String projectId)` that null-guards `getMetadata()` once; the current ternary is repeated and noisy.

findings.issue: `update_noOpRenameSameName_doesNotThrow409` correctly verifies (a) no exception is thrown, (b) project_updated event is emitted. But the verify on line 297-298 uses `anyString(), anyString(), any()` for ip/ua/metadata, which means it doesn't lock the contract that no_op rename emits metadata WITHOUT `name`/`previousName`. The neighbouring `update_noNameChange_emitsProjectUpdatedWithoutNameOrPreviousName` (line 245) does this correctly with `meta.containsOnlyKeys("projectId")`. Without metadata-shape assertion here, a regression where the service passes through `requestedName.equals(currentName)` to the rename branch (and emits `project_renamed` with `previousName==name`) could silently switch event types if the service ALSO bypassed the rename branch and emitted `project_updated` with extra fields. Minor because the noNameChange test already catches the metadata-shape regression, but the no-op-rename branch is a distinct code path (it reaches `update`'s rename-comparison logic, not the `dto.name() == null` branch).
findings.fix: Mirror the metadata assertion from line 259: `ArgumentCaptor<Map<String, Object>> meta = metadataCaptor(); verify(eventService).logEvent(eq(OWNER_ID), eq("project_updated"), eq(IP), eq(UA), meta.capture()); assertThat(meta.getValue()).containsOnlyKeys("projectId"); verify(eventService, never()).logEvent(anyString(), eq("project_renamed"), anyString(), anyString(), any());` The second verify nails down that the same-name no-op definitively does NOT enter the rename branch, distinct from the no-name-change path.

findings.issue: Empirical result for the patterns.md "three connection-factory mocks" guidance is documented in the test's class-comment, but only inline. Task 3 implementation hints (line 261) explicitly asked: "Document the empirical result (mocks needed: 0 / 1 / 3) in the post-completion report." The result here is **zero mocks needed** — same as `AuthControllerSliceTest`. This is useful intel: patterns.md line 38 ("Spring Boot 3.5.x requires three mocks to prevent auto-config from connecting to live databases") may be stale or scoped narrower than written. Two slice tests now exist that contradict it.
findings.fix: Two small writeups, one in each direction. (1) In `decisions.md` for this feature, add a one-liner: "Slice test ProjectControllerSliceTest passes with 0 connection-factory @MockitoBean entries (only ProjectService is mocked). Matches AuthControllerSliceTest precedent. Confirms patterns.md line 38's three-mock guidance is more conservative than necessary for `@WebFluxTest(controllers=...)` slice tests in this codebase." (2) In `.claude/skills/project-knowledge/references/patterns.md` line 38, soften the wording from "requires three mocks" to "may require up to three mocks if the controller's transitive dependencies trigger Mongo/Redis auto-config — verify empirically; both AuthControllerSliceTest and ProjectControllerSliceTest bootstrap with zero connection-factory mocks because @WebFluxTest disables most auto-config." Don't block this PR on the patterns.md edit — it's a project-knowledge update, separate concern. The decisions.md note alone closes the post-completion checklist item.

findings.issue: `errorBodies_alwaysHaveMessageAndCode` covers AC-T1 for three statuses (400 / 404 / 409) but skips 422 (`project_limit_reached`). 422 is a separate code-emitting branch through `AppException.unprocessableEntity(code, message)` and worth pinning in the error-body shape test. Also, the 404 arm only asserts `$.message` is non-blank — it does not assert `$.code` is null/absent (the user-spec contract for 404 is `{message, code: null}` per AC-T1 + tasks/3.md line 138 "For 404 use AppException.notFound(...) (single-argument is fine here — code = null is acceptable for 404"). A regression where 404 starts emitting `code: "project_not_found"` would slip through.
findings.fix: Append a fourth arm covering 422: seed 5 active projects, attempt 6th, assert `expectStatus().isEqualTo(422)` + `$.message` non-blank + `$.code == "project_limit_reached"`. And tighten the 404 arm to also assert `$.code` is null or absent: replace the current 404 block with `.expectStatus().isNotFound().expectHeader().contentTypeCompatibleWith(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).expectBody().jsonPath("$.message").value(s -> assertThat((String) s).isNotBlank()).jsonPath("$.code").doesNotExist();` (or `.isEqualTo(null)` depending on which Jackson serialization is in play — check `GlobalErrorHandler.toBody(...)` to confirm whether `code = null` is omitted or included). The added assertions cost two lines and finish AC-T1 coverage end-to-end.

non_findings: TDD-anchor coverage is complete: all 20 ProjectServiceTest names, the 1 SliceTest name, and all 38 ProjectControllerIT names from tasks/3.md TDD Anchor section exist as method names on the corresponding classes — no missing tests.

Decision 14 deletedAt-FIRST guard is verified correctly in both ProjectServiceTest::restore_onActiveProject_throws404AndDoesNotEmitRenameOrRestore (uses Mockito verify(...,never()) on both event types — would fail if the service entered rename or restore branches) and ProjectControllerIT::restoreProject_onActiveProject_returns404AndDoesNotEmitRenameOrRestoreEvent (queries the events collection and asserts neither project_renamed nor project_restored exists for the active project's id). The unit-level assertion is the strict litmus test: removing the deletedAt-FIRST line in ProjectService.restore would silently let the rename branch fire, and verify(...,never(),...) would catch it.

Mass-assignment defense (Risk R2) is fully verified by postProject_hostileBodyWithOwnerId_savesAuthenticatedOwnerIdAndResponseHasNoOwnerIdField: (a) hostile body sends ownerId=OTHER_USER_ID, (b) response asserts $.ownerId.doesNotExist, (c) DB re-fetch asserts saved.getOwnerId().equals(USER_ID), (d) bonus — asserts no project was created for OTHER_USER_ID. All four arms catch distinct regressions.

Anti-enumeration parity covers all four verbs × three id-classes where applicable: GET (foreign/malformed/soft-deleted-own), PATCH (foreign/malformed/soft-deleted-own), DELETE (foreign/malformed/already-soft-deleted), POST-restore (foreign/malformed/on-active). Twelve dedicated test methods, all asserting status 404 with no other-status leakage. Decision 2's uniformity contract is locked.

409 and 422 tests assert on the `code` field, not just status — for both POST and PATCH conflict paths (project_name_taken) and for both POST and POST-restore quota paths (project_limit_reached). This is the assertion that catches the AppException.conflict(message)-vs-conflict(code, message) factory regression flagged in tasks/3.md line 252 — without code-field assertions, a one-arg conflict() call would silently null out code and the test would still pass on status alone.

Audit-event metadata is asserted at content level, not just presence: project_created asserts metadata.projectId + metadata.name; project_renamed asserts projectId + previousName + name; project_updated asserts containsOnlyKeys("projectId") (positively excluding name and previousName); project_soft_deleted asserts projectId + name; project_restored asserts projectId + name + (renamedDueToConflict on collision path) + doesNotContainKey("renamedDueToConflict") on happy path. This is the litmus-test gold standard for event-metadata contracts.

Test pyramid is healthy and matches the test-master rubric: 20 unit (Mockito, no Spring) + 1 slice (@WebFluxTest, only response-shape) + 38 integration (Testcontainers Mongo + WebTestClient). Unit tests cover business logic in isolation; IT covers all endpoints + DB writes; slice tests fill the one gap unit can't (response JSON shape with real Spring serialization). No E2E here is correct — golden path lives in frontend e2e/projects.spec.ts per tech-spec.

Test names are descriptive (verb_scenario_outcome shape), arrangement is minimal (helper methods saveActive / saveSoftDeleted / awaitEvent / findEvent are reused, not duplicated), no console output / debug println / leftover @Disabled. Test bodies stay focused: each test asserts one concern with two-to-five jsonPath/event assertions max.
